A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Video-RTS. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original Video-RTS benchmark results, ablations, a qualitative example and appendix experiments on training data, sampling seeds and another model backbone.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and analyses, including the experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same GRPO training, format and accuracy rewards, and consensus-based sparse-to-dense inference. Algorithm 1 is relocated without procedural changes.

E1.justification: Both retain CG-Bench training, LLaVA-Video training-data analyses and evaluation on Video-Holmes, MMVU, Video-MMMU, LongVideoBench and Video-MME. No task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged, including Video-R1, SFT/SFT+RL and the alternative test-time scaling methods. Newly cited VeriPO is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes the stated Video-R1 RL training budget from 4K to 24K samples. This isolated reporting change conflicts with the retained 165K+4K setting in Table 2 and other passages; it does not establish that experiments were rerun. Other evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-data, RL/TTS component and vote-count analyses, Figure 4 case study, and Appendix C seed and backbone analyses are retained. Renaming the vote-count discussion introduces no new analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain Appendix B's fixed-seed, single-run statement and Appendix C.3's five subset-sampling seeds with MMVU accuracy of 64.2 ± 0.3. No uncertainty-reporting practice or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7, Figure 3 and the qualitative example retain their results. Table 1 still reports 40.7% on Video-Holmes and 66.4% on MMVU for Video-RTS; Appendix C.4 retains the reported 1.5% MMVU improvement with InternVL-3-8B.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and definitions remain equivalent. Equation (4) renames the ground-truth answer from A_gt to A without changing the reward; no assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims of data-efficient pure RL, adaptive inference and complementary benefits remain, including the 2.4% average advantage using 3.6% of the training samples. Abstract and conclusion shortening removes repeated specifics without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 removes the interpretation that the expert-level benchmark results close the gap to Gemini 1.5 Pro and adds a summary emphasizing leadership among open-source video-reasoning methods. Mechanism explanations and Appendix A limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 removes the Video-Holmes Apache license entry and its link. Own-model implementation details, hardware, prompts and the code/model release statement remain unchanged; the added CG-Bench fragment in Appendix B repeats existing information.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add VeriPO by Li et al. and remove SILVR by Zhang et al. The broader positioning relative to SFT, RL and language-based test-time scaling is retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits shorten the abstract, method overview and conclusion, rename the vote-count discussion, and update affiliations and acknowledgments. Section order remains stable. Appendix B gains an unfinished sentence ending in 'which is a' before the existing text.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 moves from page 5 to page 6, the appendix begins directly after the references, and prompt Table 8 occupies a standalone final page. Figures and numerical table structures remain unchanged, with minor caption and spacing edits.

improvement.justification: Some wording is cleaner, but v2 introduces a further inconsistency in the central data-efficiency comparison: Section 3.2 states 24K Video-R1 RL samples while Table 2 and other passages retain 4K. The unfinished Appendix B sentence and removed Video-Holmes license link also weaken documentation. These limited regressions outweigh the editorial gains; the scientific method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
